guidelineReference: Resus Council UK Adult Basic Life Support 2021 (Choking)
title: Severe choking at a rugby stadium stands
setting: Top of stadium stands. 62M lifelong rugby fan collapsed/staggered, clutching his throat, unable to speak, breathe, or cough. Face is red and puffy.
verdictExplanation: Severe, complete airway obstruction (unable to speak, breathe, or cough). This is a time-critical life-threatening emergency. Unequivocally sick: deliver choking treatment.

er.pulseOximetry: Unrecordable - sats probe doesn't give reading

shared.danger: Height and steepness of the stadium stairs
shared.response: Responding only to voice/touch with wild panic
shared.airway: Completely obstructed by a piece of pie
shared.circulation: Tachycardic, face is cyanosed and puffy

history.history: Inhaled a piece of meat pie while celebrating a try moments ago
history.additional: His son is on scene, extremely panicked

followUp.question: What is the correct treatment sequence for a conscious adult with severe choking?

options.text: Give up to 5 sharp back blows; if unsuccessful, give up to 5 abdominal thrusts; repeat
Start cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) with 30 chest compressions immediately
Encourage him to drink water to push the obstruction down
Perform a blind finger sweep inside his mouth to hook the object out

followUp.explanation: Severe choking is managed with up to 5 back blows followed by up to 5 abdominal thrusts. CPR is only started if the patient becomes unconscious. Giving fluids or blind finger sweeps are highly dangerous and worsen obstruction.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Lean him forward. Give 5 back blows between shoulder blades. If failed, 5 abdominal thrusts. Call 999 if the object doesn't clear rapidly.
levelFlags.erNotes: Deliver back blows and abdominal thrusts. If the patient becomes unresponsive, immediately support him to the ground, call 999/expedite, and start CPR (beginning with 30 chest compressions, checking the mouth before breaths).
